key_insight: Point2Part reframes 3D part decomposition as a full-shape partitioning problem, so predicted parts are non-overlapping and together cover the entire object. This makes part segmentation more consistent and usable for downstream tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a key flaw in existing 3D part decomposition methods: parts can overlap or leave gaps, meaning the object is not cleanly divided into complete, disjoint components.
method: Formulates part decomposition as joint partitioning of the whole 3D shape instead of predicting parts independently.
Uses point prompts to guide the decomposition process toward desired parts.
Predicts parts in a way that enforces non-overlap and full coverage of the original shape.
impact: This is useful for practitioners who need reliable part-level 3D understanding, such as robotics, CAD, and scene editing. Clean partitions improve downstream tasks that depend on precise object parts.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of overlapping/gappy parts vs. clean joint partitioning

paper_title: Point2Part: Unified 3D Partitioning from Point Prompts
paper_authors: Hao-Tang Tsui, Yu-Rou Tuan, Xiaoxuan Ma, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Takaaki Shiratori
